extracted.intended_audience: Navy command and claimant-level personnel responsible for Commercial Activity (CA) cost-comparison, contract administration, and quality assurance (contracting officers, QA evaluators, claimants, program managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for implementing Navy Commercial Activity (CA) cost-comparisons, transitions to contractor operations, and post-award contract administration/quality-assurance. Focuses on performance measurement, PWS development, staffing, cost accounting, and policy/implementation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement and use of objective data
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance assessments should be based on formal measurement programs (observation, Quality Assurance inspections, external inspections, customer satisfaction measures) and include objective data comparing pre-award and post-award performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes most assessments used observation and QA inspections; only three commands provided objective pre/post performance statistics. Lack of objective data suggests need for better control systems and database management to substantiate contractor performance claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and enforcement of deduction clause for substandard performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts should include a deduction clause that permits financial deductions for substandard performance and be enforced when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 56% of commands had taken deductions (generally <1% of contract price). Anti-pattern: absence of a deduction clause led to tolerated poor performance and inability to enforce standards; enforcement requires good documentation and QA records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Contract Discrepancy Reports and corrective administrative actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands should document deficiencies with Contract Discrepancy Reports and take corrective actions such as contract clarification/amplification, sanitation discrepancy notices, and periodic performance reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four commands issued Contract Discrepancy Reports to support deductions. Other useful actions included clarifications without reimbursement and quarterly performance reviews with contractor — practical tools to remediate problems before escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor experience and prior performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer contractors experienced in the specific operation, ideally with prior Navy or DoD work, to increase chances of satisfactory performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All respondents indicated current contractors were experienced; ~67% had prior Navy/DoD experience. Failure to account for experience can increase transition problems and post-award issues (claims, litigation preparation costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement method, technical proposals, and pre-award surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Select procurement method (sealed bid, negotiated, set-aside) and require technical proposals as appropriate; perform pre-award surveys to assess prospective contractors' financial integrity and technical competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority used negotiated procurement and technical proposals. Only 44% of activities were involved in pre-award surveys. A pre-award survey is an on-site visit to assess financial and technical competence and is recommended to inform award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive cost comparison (include post-award administrative and indirect costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparison studies must account for all costs of contracting out, including contract administration, vehicles, QA staff time, negotiation time, productivity losses among remaining government employees (morale impacts), and potential post-award litigation costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents felt cost comparisons understate actual costs; examples include unanticipated contract administration costs, morale-induced productivity losses, and litigation expenses. Omitting these items can produce inaccurate assessments of savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate contract administration and QA staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure an adequate, competent contract administration and QA staffing level tailored to operation complexity (multi-function contracts require more staffing than stand-alone functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cites Cost Comparison Handbook staffing as often inadequate. For large multi-function contracts, one claimant recommended ~18-20 people headed by a Service Contract Manager (SCM). Staffing supported by a major claimant reduces implementation burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and implement a detailed Quality Assurance (QA) Plan with competent QA evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed, complete QA Plan plus competent QA personnel are critical to documenting, enforcing, and correcting deficient contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four of nine reviewed commands never implemented a QA plan; poor QA documentation undermines ability to assess deductions and defend against litigation. Investment in QA training, manuals, sampling techniques, and documentation is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow initial tolerance for minor substandard performance during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit a limited amount of substandard performance in early contract stages (transition/learning curve) without immediate deductions to foster working relations, but enforce standards after the initial period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several respondents intentionally tolerated minor deficiencies early to enhance government-contractor relations; subsequently an adequate QA staff must enforce standards after transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor contract type to operation complexity (award fee vs firm fixed price)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select contract type based on complexity: Cost-Plus-Award-Fee for complex operations requiring flexibility/incentives, Firm-Fixed-Price for less complex, stand-alone operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: award fee offers positive incentive and is not subject to litigation, reducing documentation burdens; deduction clauses are negative incentives and more litigable. Choice should reflect need for coordination and risk control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management review process (MEO) is beneficial but avoid overly lean MEOs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Management Review/Major Organizational Efficiency (MEO) process to gain efficiencies, but ensure MEOs are not so 'lean' that they cannot meet PWS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nearly all respondents found MEO helpful in achieving efficiencies; however, some warned that excessively lean MEOs may fail to satisfy performance standards and lead to contract performance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized claimant oversight, support teams, and lesson-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralized claimant or subclaimant oversight and study/implementation teams enhance successful CA implementation by providing guidance, sharing lessons learned, and minimizing reinvention at each command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COMNAVAIRPAC's implementation teams shortened transitions and reduced problems. Centralized guidance provides technical assistance in management studies, MEO, and PWS development and helps reduce litigation and rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-end planning and post-award sustainment/contingency guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop front-end plans and central policy guidance for post-decision/post-award activities, including sustaining service operations in event of contractor default or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and Naval Audit Service stress need for planning beyond cost comparison. Commands lacking contingency plans sometimes continued paying deficient contractors because alternatives were unavailable; recommended issuance of OPNAV-443 instruction for sustaining operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and completeness of the Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS must clearly and precisely define task requirements; inadequate or vague PWSs lead to performance failure, claims, inaccurate savings estimates, and costly resolicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two commands cited vague/unenforceable PWSs as contributors to contractor failure. GAO testimony noted PWS inadequacies caused cost increases and unrealized savings in multiple cases. Complex operations require greater resource allocation to develop precise PWSs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and plan for contract modification difficulty and mission changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that complex or mission-shifting operations will require contract modifications/renegotiations that are time-consuming and costly; design contracts and transition strategies to manage these risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inflexibility is a downside of contracting out for functions experiencing significant scope/mission changes; one-time special requirements cannot be quickly performed without negotiated modifications and agreed reimbursements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use implementation teams to assist field activities during cost comparison and transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Field an implementation team (claimant-level) to assist commands through CA milestones, leveraging experience and reducing transition problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COMNAVAIRPAC's implementation team model provided centralized expertise and an information network that reduced attrition impacts and shortened transition periods with fewer deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize QA manuals, sampling techniques, and training across claimancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt/adapt comprehensive QA manuals (e.g., NAVFAC model) and provide training on QA surveillance, sampling, and documentation to ensure consistent enforcement and evidence for deductions/litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only NAVFAC published a comprehensive QA manual; other claimancies would benefit from tailored adaptations. Better QA manuals and training would improve surveillance quality and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic accounting treatment of conversion costs in cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure conversion/transition costs are accounted for realistically in cost comparisons and budgeting (recognize upfront costs even if expensed over multiple years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion costs are often incurred 'up-front' but allocated over five years for expensing; this mismatch deprives commands of immediate funding credit and distorts comparisons and budget execution analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate personnel attrition through information networks and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Address attrition of CA/QA personnel by maintaining information networks, commissioning implementation teams, and providing training to preserve expertise and share lessons learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attrition was cited as a major problem. One claimant's solution was a closely linked information network and implementation teams; these measures help inexperienced staff access advice and case experience from counterparts.
